newsitem.title: GERMANY: German teens like Kohl, back SPD, trust Greenpeace.
newsitem.headline: German teens like Kohl, back SPD, trust Greenpeace.

text.p: German teenagers like Helmut Kohl as chancellor, prefer the opposition Social Democrats as a party and trust the environmentalist group Greenpeace the most among public institutions, according to a new opinion poll.

Kohl scored 25 percent support among respondents between 14 and 18 years old, a close second to President Roman Herzog and ahead of possible SPD challengers Oskar Lafontaine and Gerhard Schroeder in next year's general election, the poll showed.

But his Christian Democrats (CDU) came second in party preference with 29 percent compared with the SPD's 33 percent. The Greens, normally seen as the main youth party in Germany, scored 22 percent in the Emnid poll for the teen magazine Bravo that was broadcast on Sunday evening on N-TV television.

The poll showed young Germans trusted Greenpeace far more than any other institution, giving the environmental pressure group 63 percent support compared with 35 percent for the surprise second place winner -- the police.
Germany's courts came in third in trustworthiness at 34 percent, one point ahead of Amnesty International. Politicians were clear also-rans with only seven percent support.
In the politicians' popularity ratings, Greens party leader Joschka Fischer, 49, ranked just behind Kohl, 67, at 23 percent.

SPD chairman Lafontaine scored 18 percent while his charismatic rival Gerhard Schroeder, the Lower Saxony state premier most likely to win the mantle of the "German Tony Blair," limped in with only 12 percent support. Both are 53 years old.
Asked who was their "dream chancellor," 28 percent said "nobody." Kohl came in next at 22 percent, Lafontaine at seven percent and Schroeder at five percent.
